questions.stem: A superelastic ball is dropped from a height of 10 metres. Each time it hits the ground, it rebounds to exactly 70\% of the height from which it fell. Find the total distance the ball travels before coming to rest.
questions.hint: Calculate the first drop distance separately, and treat the subsequent upward and downward bounces as an infinite GP.

steps.explain: Identify the initial drop distance and the subsequent rebound heights.
steps.work: \(\text{First drop} = 10\text{ m}. \quad \text{Subsequent bounces involve going up and down } 70\%\text{ of the previous height.}\)

steps.explain: Write the total distance traveled as a sum of the first drop plus twice the sum of the subsequent rebounds.
Identify the parameters of the infinite geometric progression for the rebound heights.
Calculate the sum of the infinite geometric progression using the limiting sum formula.
Combine the initial drop and twice the limiting sum of rebounds to find the total distance.

questions.stem: A scholarship fund needs to provide $5000 at the end of each year for the next 15 years. If the fund earns 6\% per annum compound interest, what is the minimum lump sum that must be invested today to fund these payments?
questions.hint: Find the present value of each payment by discounting them, and sum them as a GP.

steps.explain: Represent the present value of all 15 annual payments of \(5000.\)
Identify the parameters of this geometric progression.
Apply the geometric progression sum formula.
Simplify the denominator and evaluate the expression.
Compute the final lump sum to the nearest dollar.
